decision: goal: iOS alpha of else.bot that only connects to remote servers, built on NSH
why: user asked for a mobile version for the morning; remote only, iOS first

decision: proved NSH Rust app builds and runs on the iOS simulator before writing app code
why: biggest unknown was the toolchain; hello app packaged in 3 min

decision: Rust NSH app (not TSX) in apps/mobile, own cargo workspace, reusing crates/wire
why: reuses the server's wire types and the desktop's client rules; NSH builds its own runners so it stays out of the root workspace

decision: own tokio+reqwest+tungstenite client instead of NSH fetch/websocket
why: NSH fetch follows redirects; the desktop refuses them so the owner key never leaves the saved origin; same TLS verification

decision: cross-compiled aws-lc rustls reqwest tungstenite for aarch64-apple-ios-sim
why: TLS C code was the second biggest unknown

decision: http:// only to loopback or Tailscale IPs, and only when the phone has a Tailscale interface address
why: iOS cannot run tailscale status like the desktop; a 100.x address with Tailscale off could route to carrier CGNAT

decision: dev server via scripts/dev.py with every real provider CLI pointed at /nonexistent
why: host_providers would let codex run real turns on the owner's account; only synthetic may run

decision: connect, wrong-key error, bot list, chat, send and live reply checked on the simulator against the dev server
why: the predicate is the real app on iOS against a real server
evidence: iPhone 18 Pro sim screenshots this session

decision: bot replies full width without a bubble, owner messages as bubbles
why: tables and code blocks collapsed inside a content-sized bubble; long Markdown reads better full width as in ChatGPT and Claude iOS

decision: keyboard_taps Handled on the transcript and the connect form
why: the first tap on Send or Connect only dismissed the keyboard
evidence: sim: sent with keyboard up in one tap
